answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a shared escrow before it may trade. Creating thousands of fake agents then costs real capital per identity, like hauling shale up a mountain: the summit is reachable only by paying the climb each time. Honest agents recover their stake from a common oasis of fees, while proven fakes forfeit theirs, so a Sybil flood burns its own budget instead of profiting.
